column1: # Section dispositions: authored input to the Web IDL census.
# Three tab-separated fields: <section id> <kind or *> <disposition>, resolved
# exactly as census/dispositions.tsv is for Streams, except that the heading
# ancestry runs from the innermost <h5> outward to the <h2>. Section ids are
# heading ids of vendor/whatwg-webidl-a652053f/index.bs and are case-exact.
# Seeded from the "Web IDL section dispositions" table of SPEC-MANIFEST.md as
# amended by rulings R-P4 and R-P10, and frozen row for row by section 5 of
# test/contracts/webidl-census.contract.md. Both directions are checked: an
# entry no row uses fails generation, and a row no entry reaches fails
# generation.
# The first-order exception universe Whatwg.WebIdl.Exceptions is reserved for:
# "exception", "simple exception", the five simple exception types, and the
# specification-level "create" and "throw".
idl-exceptions
# The 32 base DOMException error names, one owned data row per name under
# ruling R-P10, plus the names table that introduces them. The 22 legacy const
# members are idl rows of idl-DOMException, not rows of this section.
idl-DOMException-error-names
# Six must/should constraints on deriving an interface, stated with no
# algorithm and realized by QuotaExceededError. They enter as authored rule
# rows (census/webidl/rules.tsv) and carry disposition requirement.
idl-DOMException-derived-interfaces
# QuotaExceededError, the one predefined derived interface. Ruling R-P4 and
# the plan seat's flagged item: hostOnly, not evidenceOnly. No Streams
# algorithm reaches the name at this pin.
idl-DOMException-derived-predefineds
# Ruling R-P4 overrides the survey's recommendation of owned: the promise type
# is a type-system entry and the binding layer is hostOnly.
idl-promise
# The js-promise lead is the JavaScript-value-to-Promise<T> conversion, which
# is binding-layer.
js-promise
# The eleven promise operations DB-11 places in Whatwg.WebIdl. The pinned
# Streams source invokes them 197 times.
js-promise-manipulation
# Seven worked examples inside <div class="example"> containers, plus the
# Environment ready promise they define for illustration.
js-promise-examples
# Which host object represents each exception kind: binding, not semantics.
js-exception-objects
# The four algorithms that give "create" and "throw" their meaning.
js-creating-throwing-exceptions
# One propagation sentence; the propagation rule itself is ECMA-262's.
js-handling-exceptions
# The DOMException interface. Its associated name and message are first-order
# content Whatwg.WebIdl.Exceptions carries; its IDL surface and the interface
# type itself are the host's.
idl-DOMException
idl-DOMException
idl-DOMException
